youtube.title: What If You Played GTA 6 for 30 Days Straight? #Shorts
youtube.description:
What if you played GTA 6 for thirty days straight? No sleep. No breaks. Let's see how far you'd really get.

Hour 17: in one study, after 17-19 hours awake, people did as badly on some tests as someone at the 0.05% drink-drive limit used in many countries. Day 2: tongue twisters get hard. Day 3: memory slips, you feel sick. That's not a guess: in 1964, Randy Gardner, 17, from San Diego, stayed awake for 264 hours (about 11 days). Guinness later stopped accepting attempts at this record because it's too dangerous. And day 30? You never get there: your brain starts grabbing microsleeps, a few seconds long, whether you want them or not. When Randy finally slept, he slept about 14 hours.

The real speedrun: play, sleep, repeat. What's the longest you've ever stayed awake?

Sources:
- Williamson & Feyer (2000), Moderate sleep deprivation produces impairments in cognitive and motor performance equivalent to legally prescribed levels of alcohol intoxication, Occup Environ Med 57:649-655: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1739867
- NPR (2024), Randy Gardner and the sleep deprivation record: https://www.npr.org/2024/01/28/1227217274/sleep-deprivation-record
- Randy Gardner (record holder) overview: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Randy_Gardner_(record_holder)
- Microsleeps: NHLBI/NIH, sleep deprivation and deficiency.

Don't try this: staying awake for days is dangerous.
Remy is fictional. Not affiliated with Rockstar Games or Take-Two. No game footage, art or logos are used.
